Naegele rule and pregnancy dating: 2

A patient has a reliable last menstrual period and regular 28-day cycles. Using the conventional rule, how long after the first day is the estimated delivery date, before considering ultrasound-based revision when appropriate?

  1. 280 days from the first day of the LMP
  2. First day of the last menstrual period
  3. 17 October 2026
  4. Account for cycle length and reliability of menstrual dating
  5. Use the best obstetric estimate, including early ultrasound
Answer and explanation

280 days from the first day of the LMP

The conventional estimate assumes a 28-day cycle and ovulation around day 14.

Option explanations

280 days from the first day of the LMP: The conventional estimate assumes a 28-day cycle and ovulation around day 14.

First day of the last menstrual period: Conventional menstrual dating starts from the first day of the LMP, not the last bleeding day or presumed conception day. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

17 October 2026: Adding 280 days to 10 January 2026 gives 17 October 2026. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Account for cycle length and reliability of menstrual dating: A non-28-day or irregular cycle limits an unadjusted LMP estimate. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Use the best obstetric estimate, including early ultrasound: First-trimester ultrasound can improve dating when menstrual history is unreliable; formal redating guidance applies. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
